title: Fundamentals of Learning and Teaching of Natural Sciences
text:
The main objective of this subject is to work on the fundamental bases of science teaching. The aim is to promote science teaching-learning that promotes scientific literacy and, at the same time, encourages young people to opt for scientific careers.
The aim is to encourage reflection on the science model to be taught and the teacher’s didactic model, and also to provide the necessary tools and resources to be able to carry out the task of science teacher in accordance with current science teaching paradigms.
Key aspects in the teaching-learning of sciences are worked on; This deepens the nature of science, reflects on the importance of the teaching model of the teachers and the students’ previous ideas, on the self-regulation of learning, the role of language in the construction of knowledge, the importance of experimental or practical work and didactic activities outside the classroom and, finally, project-based learning.
The importance of modeling in science and the treatment of diversity are aspects that will be taught with the problem-based learning (PBL) methodology. The learning process begins with a problem situation that promotes the identification of learning needs. You will work with groups of 8-10 students with a tutor as a learning facilitator. The learning process is directed by the students themselves. At the end of each of the two problems, the results will be presented to the rest of the classmates.
All the contents and procedures that will be worked on in this subject will be basic resources for the design of didactic sequences that will be carried out in the DEIA subject.

7 Methodology

7.1 a) Face-to-face sessions

The sessions will be theoretical-practical, activities to work in the classroom will be combined with presentations by the teachers. Active learning methodologies will therefore predominate and reflective practice will be facilitated.
A good part of the tasks that will be carried out in person during classes will be carried out working in cooperative groups.
Some of the topics of this subject are worked with the problem-based learning methodology.
The student will have at their disposal on the virtual platform the presentations and documents used during the sessions and complementary information on each topic.



7.2 b) Non-face-to-face tasks

Students will have various documents at their disposal on the Virtual Platform that will be used to prepare different tasks (individual or group); These tasks must contribute to achieving the objectives of the subject.



7.3 c) Practical sessions

During the course there will be some practical sessions in the laboratories of the Faculty of Health and Life Sciences (FCSV). Students will be required to wear a gown for these sessions. There will also be a field trip to Collserola that will take place in the morning.



7.4 d) Scheduled visits

Two trips will be made to scientific institutions where educational activities are carried out for secondary school students, with the aim of learning about the resources that these types of centers offer for students and teachers of natural sciences and working on how to make good use of them.

title: Master’s Final Project
text:
In the Master of Teacher Training in Compulsory Secondary Education and Baccalaureate, Vocational Training and Language Teaching, the student must develop a Master’s Final Project (TFM) under the supervision of the university tutor. The workload involved in this work is 6 credits (ECTS), which approximately corresponds to 150 hours of student work.
The Master’s Final Project is understood as an exercise of synthesis, integration and deepening of all the knowledge and skills acquired during the master’s degree, and consists of the development of a topic in depth and exhaustively. This topic must necessarily be of interest to the student and related to the teaching practice of their specialty. The focus of this work must be fundamentally the bibliographic exploration, the analysis of the situation in the classroom during the practicum and the formulation, application and analysis of the impact of innovative educational and didactic proposals in the context of the internship educational center.
During the development of the TFM, the student must connect the topic on which he develops the work with the contents covered in the generic module and the specialization module, as well as with everything he has seen and learned in the practicum stay.

text:
6 Methodology

The final master’s thesis (TFM) consists of carrying out an action research to introduce an improvement in some aspect related to science classes in secondary school, always within the framework of the units and/or didactic sequences designed in DEIA.
The TFM will be carried out with the internship couple or individually.
During the first internship at an educational center, the student must focus on some aspect that could be improved in science classes and develop one or more research questions.
Throughout the DEIA sessions and independent work, a bibliographic search on the topic will be carried out and educational actions that will supposedly lead to an improvement in science classes will be designed. During the second internship, within the framework of the teaching units and/or sequences that the student implements with the groups of students that the mentor has assigned to him/her, the educational actions linked to the TFM will be carried out, and the results will be observed and data collected.
Subsequently, the analysis of these data should allow us to assess whether or not the didactic intervention carried out represents an improvement in science classes, answering the research question initially posed and allowing the elaboration of the conclusions of the TFM.
Throughout the entire process of completing the TFM, two joint tutorials will be carried out by the tutor and his or her group of students to assess their development and carry out co-evaluation actions. Individualized tutorials can also be carried out with the tutor.
The presentation of the TFM will be done through a written report that will be delivered electronically and its defense will be carried out in a poster session at the end of the course.

title: Master’s Final Project
text:
7 Assessment

To be able to present the TFM, it is recommended to have positively passed the evaluation of the subjects of the fundamentals of secondary education and teaching specialization modules, and it is mandatory to obtain a positive grade in the evaluation of the practicum. If the practicum has been suspended, the defense of the TFM will be done the following academic year, with the same calendar as the rest of the students and always depending on the completion of the practicum.
The student will make a first delivery of the TFM, which will be reviewed by the tutor and a referee (external reviewer). These will review the different parts of the TFM and, if appropriate, make proposals for improvement, and will recommend or not accept it. From this moment, students have one week to make the necessary amendments and send the final version of the TFM.
In the month of June, the presentations of the TFMs of all specialties will take place. They will be presented in person in public poster sessions. The TFM will be evaluated by a Tribunal made up of three Master’s professors, through the written report and its public oral defense. This court must include the student’s mentor and the University tutor. Thus, the TFM evaluation panel will be made up of: the center’s mentor/tutor, the university tutor and a master’s professor from the university.


7.1 Evaluation weighting

TFM written memory (70%)
Oral presentation of the TFM poster (30%)

The objective of the UPF master’s degree in teaching is to train competent professionals prepared for the current and future challenges of education. Throughout the course, you will work on the key competencies to be a teacher and you will review and mature both the conceptions of teaching-learning and the nature of the knowledge of your specialty, sharing the experience with your course mates.
This master’s degree has a globalized and holistic approach, with experiential, collaborative learning based on reflective practice. Participation in the practicum in centers and the support of mentors are a key piece of professional growth, complemented by classes at the university, online and in person.
These are the seven areas of competence that you will work on transversally in the different subjects. As a professionalizing master’s degree, these areas cover the various aspects of the teaching task: communication, management, guidance, research and reflection on personal practice, in addition to the design of the apprentices’ learning sequences. The evidence of the acquisition of these skills will be collected in the projects and activities that you will do in the subjects, in the practicum portfolio and in the master’s thesis.

This is a group activity. This activity aims to analyze the ESO science curriculum, it will be carried out in groups and will be evaluated through an oral presentation that each of the groups will make.



8.2 Task 2: Assessment of disciplinary knowledge (35%)

Knowledge of each discipline will be assessed through the completion of a collaborative exam.

Phase 1: Each student must individually take a written test. The student must answer in writing the questions related to the two blocks they have taken. Teachers will collect the written work.
Phase 2: Immediately following phase 1, groups of 4-5 students will be formed (according to the teachers’ instructions). Each group will share and argue the individual answers and will answer the questions again in a single document that the teachers will also collect.
Phase 3: Each student will work individually again and do a metacognitive regulation.


8.3 Task 3: Evaluation of didactic knowledge of scientific disciplines (30%)

In groups formed by students who take the same block.
Each group must write a proposal for a teaching-learning activity on the topic and level indicated, consistent with the secondary school curriculum and that mobilizes the contents and resources worked on in the corresponding disciplinary block. Hello, I am Pedro Martínez Durán - Senior Petroleum Geologist and passionate FullStack WebGIS Developer with more than 25 years of international experience in geosciences, exploration, geospatial analysis and management.
I obtained a BSc in Geology from the University of Zaragoza (Spain) in 1993, studying the last two years at the University of Burgundy (France) and the University of Aberdeen. I later obtained an M.Phil. in carbonate sedimentology and sequence stratigraphy at the University of Zaragoza, publishing several articles.
For some years, I developed my career as a mining exploration geologist (working in Chile, Argentina, Bolivia, USA, Türkiye, Portugal, France and Italy). ESIC’s MBA and Master in Marketing and Sales led me to various management positions for almost 8 years as CEO in three positions. Finally, this degree in management was completed with the PDG from IESE in 2007. In 2010 I returned to geology, becoming a petroleum geologist after completing the M.Sc. in Petroleum Geosciences at Royal Holloway in 2011.
I was based in the UK for 14 years as a petroleum exploration geologist and seismic interpreter working at CGG. My role focused on studies related to Reservoir Geology, Carbon Capture and H2 Storage, involving seismic interpretation of 3D and 2D regional studies at a regional scale, carrying out the complete structural analysis, seismic interpretation of the pre- and syn-rift packages and salt basins in North and West Africa, North Sea, Gulf of Mexico, New Zealand, Australia, as well as in the evaluation of several blocks in Asia, and complex unitization processes of oil fields in Algeria and Tunisia.
In recent years, I have completed internal and external training in geographic information techniques, especially with Remote Sensing datasets using ArcGIS Pro and Google Earth Engine programming in JavaScript along with training in SQL and Python to address complex geographic data sets and carry out any type of analytical approaches.
This extensive international experience has provided personal and work skills in any environment, such as critical thinking, problem solving, collaborative skills, strong emotional intelligence, cognitive flexibility and decision making focused on customer service and negotiation skills.

title: About this site
text:
This guide provides a complete walkthrough to create and publish a Quarto website to GitHub Pages using GitHub Actions for automated deployment.


Before you begin, make sure you have:

Git installed on your computer (Download Git)
Quarto installed (Download Quarto)
A GitHub account (Sign up for GitHub)
A text editor or IDE (VS Code, RStudio, etc.)






Open your terminal and run:
quarto create project website mywebsite
cd mywebsite
This creates a basic Quarto website structure with:

_quarto.yml - Configuration file
index.qmd - Home page
about.qmd - About Page
styles.css – Custom styles




Edit _quarto.yml to customize your site. Here is an example configuration:
project:
  type: website
  output-dir: _site

website:
  title: "Mi Sitio Web"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Inicio
      - about.qmd

format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
    css: styles.css
    toc: true
Key configuration options:

output-dir: Where rendered files are saved (default: _site)
title: The title of your website
theme: Choose from Bootswatch themes
navbar: Navigation structure




Test your website locally before publishing:
quarto preview
This opens a live preview on http://localhost:4200 that updates automatically when you make changes.






In your project directory:
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Commit inicial: Sitio web Quarto"



Create a .gitignore file to exclude unnecessary files:
/.quarto/
/_site/
/.Rproj.user/
*.Rproj
.DS_Store
The _site directory will be generated by GitHub Actions, so we do not confirm it.







Go to GitHub and sign in
Click the “+” icon in the upper right corner
Select “New repository”
Enter the repository details:

Repository name: mywebsite (or your preferred name)
Description: Optional description
Visibility: Public (required for free GitHub Pages)
DO NOT initialize with README, .gitignore, or license

Click “Create repository”




Creating a new repository on GitHub





Copy the commands from GitHub (shown after creating the repository):
git remote add origin https://github.com/tunombredeusuario/mywebsite.git
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main
Replace yourusername with your actual GitHub username.







Go to your repository on GitHub
Click the “Settings” tab
Scroll down to “Pages” in the left sidebar
Under “Source”, select “GitHub Actions”




GitHub Pages Setup


This tells GitHub to use GitHub Actions for deployment instead of a branch.






In the root of your project, create the GitHub Actions workflow directory:
mkdir -p .github/workflows



Create .github/workflows/publish.yml with the following content:
name: Publish Quarto Website

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: "pages"
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Quarto
        uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
        with:
          version: 'release'

      - name: Render Quarto Project
        run: quarto render

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: _site

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4



Workflow components:

on: push: branches: [main]: Activated with pushes to the main branch
workflow_dispatch: Allow manual activation from the GitHub interface
permissions: Permissions required for deployment to GitHub Pages
concurrency: Prevents multiple deployments from running simultaneously
build job: Download code, install Quarto, render site
deploy job: Deploy the rendered site to GitHub Pages

Key actions used:

actions/checkout@v4: Download your repository
quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2: Install Quarto
actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3: Upload the site for deployment
actions/deploy-pages@v4: Deploy to GitHub Pages







Add and commit the workflow file:
git add .github/workflows/publish.yml
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "Añadir flujo de trabajo de GitHub Actions para despliegue"
git push




Go to your repository on GitHub
Click the “Actions” tab
You should see your workflow running




Running GitHub Actions workflow



Click the workflow run to view detailed logs
Wait for the build and deploy jobs to complete (usually 1-3 minutes)




Once the deployment is successful, your website will be available at:
https://tunombredeusuario.github.io/mywebsite/
Replace yourusername with your GitHub username and mywebsite with the name of your repository.






If you have your own domain, you can use it instead of the default GitHub Pages URL:

Go to Settings → Pages in your repository
Under “Custom domain”, enter your domain (e.g. www.mysite.com)
Click “Save”




Add DNS records with your domain provider:
For apex domain (mysite.com):
A     185.199.108.153
A     185.199.109.153
A     185.199.110.153
A     185.199.111.153
For subdomain (www.mysite.com):
CNAME     tunombredeusuario.github.io
More details: GitHub Pages Custom Domain Documentation






Edit any .qmd file in your project:
# Editar archivos
nano index.qmd

# Previsualizar cambios
quarto preview



Commit and upload your changes:
git add .
git commit -m "Actualizar contenido"
git push
GitHub Actions will automatically rebuild and redeploy your website in minutes.








Solution: Make sure workflow permissions are set correctly:

Go to Settings → Actions → General
Under “Workflow permissions”, select “Read and write permissions”
Check “Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests”
Click “Save”




Solution: Verify that:

The GitHub Pages feed is set to “GitHub Actions”
Workflow completed successfully
You are using the correct URL format
The repository is public (for free GitHub Pages)




Fix: This usually occurs with incorrect base paths. Update _quarto.yml:
website:
  site-url: "https://tunombredeusuario.github.io/mywebsite"
  repo-url: "https://github.com/tunombredeusuario/mywebsite"



Solution:

Make sure the workflow file is in the .github/workflows/ directory
Verify that the file has the .yml or .yaml extension
Confirm that you pushed to the main branch
Try activating it manually: Actions → Workflow name → Run workflow








If your Quarto documents use R or Python code:


Update .github/workflows/publish.yml to include the R configuration:
- name: Set up R
  uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2

- name: Install R packages
  run: |
    install.packages(c("rmarkdown", "knitr", "tidyverse"))
  shell: Rscript {0}



Update .github/workflows/publish.yml to include the Python configuration:
- name: Set up Python
  uses: actions/setup-python@v5
  with:
    python-version: '3.11'

- name: Install Python packages
  run: |
    pip install jupyter matplotlib pandas numpy




For complex computations, use Quarto’s freeze function to avoid re-executing code on each deployment:
In _quarto.yml:
execute:
  freeze: auto
This caches the computational results locally. Confirm the _freeze/ directory:
git add _freeze/
git commit -m "Añadir computaciones congeladas"

✅ Create a Quarto website locally
✅ Set up a Git repository
✅ Create a repository on GitHub
✅ Configure GitHub Pages

✅ Deploy and update your website
✅ Fix common problems

Every time you push changes to your main branch, GitHub Actions will automatically rebuild and redeploy your website. This creates a seamless publishing workflow that requires no manual intervention.
Happy publishing! 🚀

Hello, I’m Pedro and I’m studying a master’s degree in secondary school teaching at Pompeu Fabra University. This website is a record of my learning and reflection process during this master’s degree. Since my years as a free time instructor and later summer camp director, I have always been curious about the profession of educator, but life for many years has taken me down multiple paths.
Upon returning after 14 years working in England, teaching was one of my first options to reinvent myself upon my return home.
I recently saw a movie, one of those not very famous ones, but with a great message. That film is Lunana, a yak at school and there is a central phrase about the impact of the teacher that said: “Teachers can touch the future” and the truth is that it had a great impact on me and now after embarking on this process I have realized that it can be like that, and that education is one of the most powerful tools to transform lives.
So here I am, reinventing myself once again to become a good educator and be able to reverse all my life experience and scientific knowledge that I have been acquiring all these years as a mining exploration geologist, later a company director and return to explore hydrocarbons for more than half the world in the future of our society, our children.

title: Society, Family and Education
text:
This subject addresses the organizational and psycho-pedagogical foundations of the educational function in the Catalan community. On the one hand, it presents the educational system, the educational centers in which the activity takes place (institutes, school institutes, centers that provide vocational training, adult training centers, official language schools and others) and their interrelation with the family and social environment, influencing the current conception of teaching-learning and the various profiles of the students (age, cognitive development, sociocultural and economic aspects). Aspects are included such as the functions and duties of the teacher and the apprentice, access to the exercise of the teaching function or the main organizational features of the centers (departments of disciplines or subjects, teaching staff, coordination, evaluation cycles, etc.).
On the other hand, it also focuses on the daily management of the classroom, emphasizing the organization of teaching and classes, the adaptation of the curriculum to the center and each group of students, the articulation of technological resources, educational guidance and tutorial action, the promotion of student well-being and the prevention and attention of violence and personalization of learning. It is about knowing both the structural, functional and regulatory organization of secondary education as well as knowing how to facilitate coexistence between the various agents and knowing how to foresee and resolve conflicts.
The subject does not presuppose prior knowledge of the student, but hopes to take advantage of previous personal experience as a student (in secondary school, high school, etc.) and even as an occasional teacher (substitute, private classes, etc.). Also, given the rapid social and technological changes that are occurring in recent years, this subject hopes to offer practical tools and reflections based on real cases to better prepare students for the changing present and unforeseen future.
The subject has a value of 10 ECTS, which represents 260 hours of student work, with 30 face-to-face sessions of two hours (60 hours), taught in face-to-face and virtual synchronous and asynchronous mode. It is taught, above all, before making the second visit to the center, when you will have to take classes, in order to equip you with all the knowledge and skills necessary to do it well.

3 Key Questions

title: Practicum
text:
The main purpose of the practicum of the Master of Secondary Education Teacher Training is the acquisition of skills related to professional practice, in addition to being a space to put into practice and synthesize in action the knowledge acquired in the other subjects. The practicum must involve professional construction experience.
The practicum is dedicated to observation and participation in a secondary school and to reflection on its reality and on the student’s educational action. This is the first contact with the profession, and it is the time to recognize models of action, contrast theoretical reflections with real practice, as well as to ask questions about one’s own ideas and skills.
We must be aware that we are witnessing the reality of the activity of teaching and learning, not a sample of what would be ideal, of perfection; that the mentors and the rest of the professionals that you will find in the centers are “people” with their personal, family, and work problems.
It is important to take advantage of the opportunity offered to us to learn about and reflect on aspects that should be improved in educational centers. You will be the future professionals, who will soon find yourself practicing in a center like the one that now welcomes you as observers; You are, therefore, the first interested in taking advantage of all the knowledge that you will acquire in this course to write evaluations and reflections that help us make and apply proposals for improvement to the educational system.

text:
6 Work Plan
The practicum will be distributed in two periods and will be structured in three phases:

Observation phase (25 hours of dedication)
Accompanied intervention phase (75 hours of dedication)
Autonomous intervention phase (150 hours of dedication)

The first phase and part of the second will be carried out during the first period of the practicum. The final part of the second phase and the entirety of the third will be carried out during the second period of the practicum.

6.1 Meetings with the mentor

At the beginning of each of the phases, students will meet with their mentor and the Center’s practicum coordinator to plan the tasks they will carry out during this stage. The planning must include all the tasks required in the practicum work plan.



6.2 Observation phase

This period has the purpose of making a global analysis of the center, its model of educational and management practice and its relationship with the environment, as well as establishing a first contact with the life of the center and the classroom.

Specific tasks that must be performed during this phase:

Attend the mentor’s classes.
Attend Department coordination meetings.
Attend coordination meetings of teachers from different areas of the same level.
Consult the mentor about what topics the learning situations can be developed.



6.3 After the observation phase

After the observation phase, you must begin to design a teaching sequence of at least 4-5 sessions for high school (2-3 if you work individually) and a complete teaching unit for ESO, of a minimum of 8 sessions (6 sessions if you work individually), which will be taught during the autonomous intervention phase.



6.4 Accompanied intervention phase

In this period, the student begins by carrying out specific interventions in the classroom with the support and supervision of the mentor and the monitoring and reflection of the master’s tutor. In addition to the specific tasks assigned, the student must actively participate in the mentor’s classes and, if possible, in others at the center. During the first days of this second phase (still in the first quarter of the course), the student will agree with his mentor on the specific topic of the programming units, which he will design and apply later (autonomous intervention phase). Also during this phase you must know and become familiar with the groups of students in which you will take your classes during the autonomous intervention phase.

Specific tasks that must be done during this phase:

Propose and teach a minimum of two activities in the mentor’s classes and assess their development. The student must select a minimum of two activities from all the resources that have been provided in the teaching specialization module and adapt them to the mentor’s classes. If possible, it is recommended that the two activities be diverse, such as experimental practices, TAC activities, debate activities, role-playing games, among others.
Participate in an outing outside the classroom if it coincides with the internship calendar.
Correct some of the exercises that the students have done: Agree with the mentor on the correction criteria. Make an analysis of the results obtained. Carry out a training return to the students.
Attend evaluation meetings (if possible)
Attend Department coordination meetings
Attend coordination meetings of teachers from different areas of the same level.
Participate in some tutoring sessions with the entire class group.
Attend a tutor coordination meeting
Attend some meetings with families. (if possible)
Attend some individualized tutoring meetings with students.
Agree with the mentor, before the end of the first period of stay at the center, on the contents to be taught in the third phase of the practicum, that is, the specific topics of the high school teaching sequence and the ESO teaching unit.



6.5 Autonomous intervention phase

The main objective of this phase is to bring to the classroom the didactic sequences that have been designed in agreement with your mentor and the university tutor, with everything that entails: monitoring, evaluation and acting as a teacher responsible for the class group, making the corresponding decisions to manage the classroom.
In addition to the implementation of these didactic sequences, throughout this phase, the student will continue to participate and collaborate in the same type of activities that they developed throughout the accompanied intervention phase (attendance at meetings, attending activities outside the center, helping the mentor with correction tasks, etc.). Likewise, it will carry out those actions that allow it to obtain data from the action research cycle linked to the preparation of the final master’s thesis (TFM).

title: Practicum
text:
7 The Portfolio

7.1 Characteristics

The portfolio is a collection of information and documentation representative of a learning process. It is a training instrument that includes analysis and reflection on the actions that have been carried out and the design of improvement plans, basic elements that enable self-learning and continued training in the professional future.
At the same time, it is also an instrument of accreditation, since it allows the person who is learning to show what they have learned and how they have learned it in a very personal and complete way, documenting it with representative material.
During the practicum, the student must prepare a portfolio that, as its main objective, must show the development of the teaching professional’s basic skills, which he or she will put into practice during his or her stay at the teaching center. The portfolio is a good instrument to facilitate and demonstrate the development of these skills, both in the initial training period you are in, and in your future practice and professional promotion.
The portfolio presentation format will be electronic and will be done with a Google site.
In this link you can copy the pre-established structure from a template. A document will be posted in the virtual classroom with all the details of the portfolio startup procedure and its functionalities.



7.2 Elaboration

The portfolio will be made during the two periods of stay at the internship center, with deliveries at different times, which will correspond to the tasks that will be carried out in each phase of the practicum according to the specific work plan in each case. You must have completed the entire portfolio at the end of the autonomous intervention phase.



7.3 Structure
The portfolio will collect different tasks that are carried out with the support of different subjects:







Tasks
Subject where you work




1. My Practicum center
Practicum (seminars)


2. The story of the Practicum
Practicum (seminars)


3. The Practicum inquiry journal

5. A video recording of the student’s intervention in the classroom, self-assessed and co-assessed by a classmate

6. A personal assessment of how basic teaching skills have been developed during the practicum

7.4 1. My practice center

During the observation phase, a brief description of the center where the Practicum is carried out must be included in the portfolio. Emphasis will be placed on the personal vision of the master’s student, answering the following questions: What image did you take away from the internship center during the observation phase? How is it similar to the center where you studied and how is it different?



7.5 2. The story of the Practicum

During the observation phase of the Practicum, a brief story will be given about a relevant event that has been experienced at the internship center, with the aim of becoming familiar with the use of narrative records for reflective practice. This will be analyzed in one of the Practicum seminars and will be incorporated into the portfolio, after having worked on it in class.



7.6 3. Inquiry diary

The inquiry diary will be carried out throughout the period of the practicum and has the objective of developing the reflective capacity of future teachers as a tool to better understand the teaching and learning processes, and know how to use this knowledge to improve their teaching practices and innovate. It will be done in electronic format, through a template available in the e-portfolio. The different phases of the diary will be worked on in the DEIA sessions.



7.7 4. The two learning situations

During the autonomous intervention phase, the two learning situations designed and implemented in the classroom during this practice phase must be attached to the portfolio.



7.8 5. Video recording of the intervention in the classroom

During the intervention phase of the practicum, it will be necessary to record some class sessions, those that seem most representative. At the end of this phase, some fragments of the recordings must be selected, whether they are good or problematic moments, that are representative of communication and constructive interaction in the classroom and of the didactic model and methodological options. It’s not just about showing the perfect moments, but also those that we would like to comment on. It is advisable to select between 3 and 5 moments of about 3-4 minutes and make an edit of a maximum of 15 minutes.
The videos will be worked on in the last seminar of the Practicum and must be attached to the portfolio along with a self-assessment and a co-assessment.



7.9 6. Personal assessment of the development of teaching skills

During the first seminar of the practicum, a table will be made to explain the initial personal assessment of teaching competencies. In the last seminar, based on the experiences lived in the second phase of practices, a contrast will be made between this initial assessment and the final vision of the degree of personal development of teaching competencies. This contrast will be guided by the practicum evaluation rubric and will have a maximum length of two pages. This writing must state:

What has been learned and how it has been learned. Refers to the specific aspects of each competence that have been learned during this period and the activity/s that have facilitated this learning.
The strong points or aspects that have been most achieved in each competition.
The weak points or aspects to improve in the future of each competition.
The attempts at improvement made. Refers to the improvements made during the months of the practicum.
Evidence to document the statements made in the competency assessment report. It is good to relate, above all, the strengths and improvements referred to with representative material that confirms them. This material can be material that has already been previously attached to the portfolio (resources used, learning situations, video recording) or any other evidence that you consider appropriate.

title: Practicum
text:
8 Evaluation, Monitoring and Feedback

The evaluation of the practicum will be carried out from the centers where the students carry out the two internship periods and by the university tutors. During the two phases of practicum, the mentor and students will sign a table weekly showing the tasks completed and the hours of attendance at the center.


8.1 e-Portfolio (50%)

It will be evaluated by the UPF tutor and the regularity of the contributions made will be taken into account overall, as well as the quality of the reflections in the different sections (see details in the specific section of the e-Portfolio). If at any time the portfolio does not contain all the materials required to demonstrate the achievement of teaching competencies, the practicum tutor will notify the student so that they can correct it.
The presentation of the portfolio will be a requirement to be able to pass the practicum and propose the Final Master’s Thesis (TFM).
Each student will have a tutor from the university, who will be in charge of monitoring the practicum and will provide support in preparing the portfolio. Throughout the practicum period there will be continuous monitoring of the tutor through the e-portfolio. In addition, there will be a series of sessions scheduled throughout the course, called Practicum Seminars where all aspects related to the Practicum and the tasks that must be incorporated into the e-portfolio will be discussed.



8.2 Internships in an educational center (50%)

They will be evaluated by the practicum mentor and will be based on the development of teaching competencies, described in the practicum evaluation rubric.
The university tutor will visit the student to observe how he or she carries out one or more class sessions during the second internship. This visit is intended to provide feedback to the student but does not have any weight in the overall grade of the practicum.

The two key objectives of this subject are:

Give relevance to reflective practice in teaching and the teacher’s daily life as a method of transforming reality and improving teaching-learning processes.
Learn the process of designing and evaluating learning situations based on the current didactic model, and contextualized in the competency-based work curriculum.
The achievement of the first objective, which involves learning the systematization of the reflective process, will lead students to develop the role of teacher-researcher who promotes teaching innovation.
In the case of the second key objective of the subject, its achievement must allow students to be competent in the process of programming the different subjects and designing the corresponding sessions, essential to carry out the teaching task.
Some of the contents covered are continuation, expansion and application of aspects started during the first quarter in the subject of Fundamentals of Learning and Teaching of natural sciences.
The practical approach of the activities that the students will carry out will be prioritized, so that the final task of the subject will be the tutored preparation of two of the three final products of the master’s degree: a learning situation for ESO and a learning situation for high school, as well as the design and implementation of an action research in the classroom, which will be put into practice during the second phase of the practicum, which will allow the students to prepare their final master’s thesis (TFM). Whenever possible, students will develop, apply and evaluate the teaching materials and educational actions developed within the framework of these two final products in the classroom in pairs.

7 Methodology

7.1 a) Theoretical-practical sessions

This subject has a very practical nature and is closely related to the practicum. The classes are designed so that students incorporate knowledge into their teaching practices.
The sessions will be of a practical-theoretical nature, which means that students will be constantly confronted with concrete learning experiences and activities, from the reflection of which theoretical knowledge will gradually be built.
In several of the face-to-face sessions, accompanied work will be carried out to prepare the programming, materials and didactic interventions, which make up the final products of the subject and the master’s degree (a learning situation in high school, a learning situation for ESO and an action research of didactic innovation), which will subsequently be taken to the classroom during the second phase of the practicum.
The internship work groups, that is, those students who will design and apply these products together, will be formed from the beginning of the master’s degree and based on the allocation of places to carry out the internships at the educational center.



7.2 b) Non-face-to-face tasks

Students will have various documents at their disposal on the virtual Platform. A good part of these tasks will be directed towards the elaboration of the different parts of the high school didactic sequence and the ESO unit. The other non-face-to-face tasks, which will be prepared in the students’ e-portfolio, will allow the action research cycle aimed at introducing a didactic innovation to be carried out: presentation and discussion of the inquiry question, analysis of an article that bases the innovation and presentation of the action plan.



7.3 c) Oral presentations

At the end of the third quarter of the master’s degree, after having experienced the high school learning situation and the ESO learning situation in the classroom, and carrying out the action research in the classroom, an oral presentation of the results will be given. In these presentations, students must make a synthesis of the didactic characteristics and activities of the ESO unit, as well as a special emphasis on the analysis of the results obtained and the proposals for improvement that they consider relevant. Likewise, this presentation will present the results and conclusions obtained from the didactic innovation introduced during the action research.
